name: Stinson SR Reliant
summary: 1930s four-to-five-seat cabin monoplane with a distinctive gull-wing from the SR-7 onward; about 1,300 were built, civil and military.

wings: SR-7 and later have a gull wing, thickest and broadest at mid-span, with one strut per side
engines: Round radial engine (Lycoming, Wright, Jacobs or Pratt & Whitney) under a cowl
fuselage: Enclosed cabin with large side windows seating four or five
Visible step up between the fuselage and the wing roots

tellTales: High-wing cabin monoplane with a gull-shaped wing
Single strut per side from a dipped wing root
Big radial with a tall enclosed cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Howard has a straight wing and a deeper, wider cabin; the Reliant SR-7 and later have a dipped gull wing.
The Robin has two parallel diagonal bracing struts per side; the Reliant has a single strut and a gull wing.
The Staggerwing is a biplane; the Reliant is a high-wing monoplane.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
